purpose: separate target-label scarcity from source-initialization benefit by adding matched target-only few-shot-from-scratch controls on the exact target partitions used by existing cross-domain runs

evidence_supported_conclusions: Target-only 5-shot training from scratch already recovers a large amount of the direct-transfer gap on FD001_TO_FD003.
Within the current v3 no-spec mainline, source initialization alone provides a modest gain of about 0.53 RMSE over target-only scratch on this canonical task.

The full cross-domain pipeline then adds a further gain of about 1.31 RMSE beyond source-initialized supervised finetuning, so most of the mainline advantage over scratch is not explained by source initialization alone.
Even after that gain, the remaining gap to the FD003 target oracle is still large at about 6.51 RMSE.
On FD001_TO_FD004, target-only 5-shot training from scratch already captures most of the gain over direct transfer.
On this harder task, source initialization alone provides a modest gain of about 0.90 RMSE over target-only scratch.

But the full current CD-MambAtt v2 pipeline is actually about 0.48 RMSE worse than simple source-initialized supervised finetuning, which implies the extra unlabeled/domain-adaptation machinery is slightly hurting in this matched comparison.
The remaining gap to the FD004 target oracle is still about 7.41 to 7.90 RMSE depending on whether those extra losses are used.

important_caveats: The within-task comparisons are controlled and matched by target partition; the cross-domain and target-only numbers differ mainly by whether source initialization and unlabeled/domain-adaptation machinery are present.

The FD001_TO_FD003 and FD001_TO_FD004 matched baselines come from different maintained branches (v3 no-spec versus v2 stable), so cross-task differences in transfer-init gain should be treated as suggestive rather than perfectly architecture-controlled.
project_level_takeaway: The new controls falsify the strongest version of the claim that post-MMD work was entirely useless, but they also sharpen where the value really is.
On the canonical FD001_TO_FD003 task, source initialization alone helps only modestly, while the larger extra gain comes from the full cross-domain training machinery.
On FD001_TO_FD004, source initialization still helps, but the extra unlabeled/domain-adaptation machinery is slightly harmful relative to simple source-initialized supervised finetuning.

So the correct narrower conclusion is not just that source initialization matters; it is that the value of the current cross-domain objective is task-dependent, and the remaining main ceiling is still the large gap to the target oracle.
